title: Staff-Level Platform Architecture
outcome: Defend regional platform contracts, per-cell route authority, migration gates, ownership and total cost.

steps.owner: App owner and platform control plane
steps.input: Trusted tenant and app manifest with a stable change key.
steps.output: Durable proposed change: recorded intent, not a deployment.
steps.failure: Invalid scope, budget, region or bundle rejects the proposal.

steps.owner: Shadow runner in the approved cell
steps.input: Authorised read-only samples and the pinned candidate route.
steps.output: Evidence appended and bound to the baseline route and generation.
steps.failure: A side-effectful shadow or invalid counts reject; a mismatch is never erased.

steps.owner: App and platform owners
steps.input: All evidence for the change plus current target eligibility.
steps.output: Pilot allowed: 100 or more samples, zero mismatches, same baseline.
steps.failure: Too few samples, any mismatch, stale evidence or revoked eligibility blocks.

steps.owner: Cell route authority in the regional authority store
steps.input: Signed generation N+1 pulled from the control plane; expected generation N.
steps.output: CAS moves N to N+1, keeps the previous route and appends a history row.
steps.failure: An unsigned, older or stale generation, or a pre-commit failure, leaves N intact.

steps.owner: Regional runtime
steps.input: Existing operation IDs, source policy, budgets and release.
steps.output: Customer outcomes are inspected under inherited runtime rules.
steps.failure: Routing changes cannot replay uncertain old external calls.

steps.owner: Authorised operator at the cell
steps.input: Current eligibility of the previous route, actor and reason.
steps.output: Local CAS to the previous generation; history keeps both rows.
steps.failure: A revoked previous route blocks rollback; going forward again needs a fresh change.

diagrams.title: Before: copied integration logic
diagrams.description: Four teams copy configuration around existing regional capabilities; the defect is inconsistent contracts and ownership.
nodes: A and B in EU, C in US-home
Request, retrieval, job and serving contracts
Metadata, sources, audit, evaluation and registry

diagrams.title: After: versioned platform contracts
diagrams.description: A control plane validates manifests and signs route generations; each cell keeps its own route authority and existing regional services enforce runtime safety. The control plane does not process prompts.
nodes: Versioned manifest, tests and accountable owner
Validate manifests and sign route generations
Proposal, bound shadow evidence and generation gate
Route records in the regional authority store
Identity, jobs, retrieval, serving and budgets
History, audit, usage and model lineage

diagrams.title: Migration sequence
diagrams.description: Propose, compare, review, cut over at the cell, observe, and roll back only if the previous route is currently eligible. Failed evidence or a revoked target blocks at review and keeps the current route.
nodes: Control plane records the change; intent only
Shadow evidence bound to baseline route and generation
Gate: 100 samples, zero mismatches, current eligibility
Cell pulls signed generation; CAS N to N+1
Serve under one generation; enforce access and operation identity
Local CAS to the previous generation with actor and reason, if eligible

controls.label: Shared operations and support (hours a month)

lab_title: Does the platform repay its migration cost?
lab_assumptions: Illustrative $100 an hour labour, 120 baseline hours a month, $1,000 a month incremental control infrastructure and $20,000 a month common serving. During overlap months both the duplicated work and the platform are paid. No discounting, tax or revenue estimate.
